title: 03 — Working with the AI

English | Português (Brasil)

03 — Working with the AI

Up to here, everything the kit did could have been done by hand (and it was — that's why nobody did it). The difference starts now: the MeuApp workspace is prepared for an AI to work inside it, conducting the workflow. This tutorial opens Opencode in the workspace and runs the first real cycle.

Opening Opencode in the workspace

cd MinhaOrganizacao\MeuApp
opencode

What the AI sees when opening is not the bare workspace. The golmet install --engine opencode (tutorial 00) materialized the complete workflow into the engine config — and the engine, opening in the workspace, loads:

  • the AGENTS.md — the workflow page the AI reads first: the primaries by domain (who conducts requirements, who conducts docs, who conducts dev), the gm-* skills by trigger ("WHEN eliciting requirements, read this"), the organization's rules and the knowledge router;
  • the delegation architecture — the AI knows gm-req conducts business discovery, that gm-dev coordinates implementation with executors and QA, that nothing edits REQUIREMENTS.md without going through the requirement cycle.

That is why the recommended mode is FULL + Opencode: in FULL, the 93 workflow components (agents, skills, profiles, templates) are in the engine. With the essential profile, the 16 BASE skills live versioned in the workspace's .golmet/ zone — the workflow works on any engine, with the base subset.

The first requirement, with the AI

The client asked: "the booking needs slot confirmation — the client reserves, has 15 minutes to confirm, or the slot is released". João, the dev, opens Opencode and talks:

"The slot-confirmation requirement needs to enter MeuApp — reservation with a 15-minute confirmation window."

The gm-clarify skill steps in. It doesn't swallow the request: it questions — what's the no-show policy? What happens to the payment if the slot is released? The 15 minutes count from which mark? Each ambiguity becomes a scored question; what the client confirms becomes a requirement, what stays open becomes a PEND with a dated follow-up.

When the score closes, gm-req writes the section into REQUIREMENTS.md:

## RN-001 — Booking with slot confirmation

state: confirmed

The client confirms the reservation within 15 minutes ...

Born confirmed — because it came from the product owner. When the code implements it, the state rises to active with evidence: the file, the line and the commit hash.

The real cycle

From here the journey continues on its own — and that is the next tutorial: 04 — the cycle of one feature walks a whole feature (requirement → spec → task → code → validation → delivery) with each document showing up at the moment it is created. The full map of who is born from whom is in docs/concepts/artefatos.md.

What matters here: the AI doesn't invent the process — it executes it. The skills have a contract (FORMAT §10): they know what they may write, what needs operator confirmation, and when to degrade. The project's state remains declared in documents humans read — the AI is the engine, not the owner.
